miniProject.title: Composed parallel plan with tested critical path
miniProject.brief: Extend trainlab with a mesh planner that turns a world size into legal parallel layouts with predicted memory and step time. Validate every ledger against CPU collectives and independent oracles, and freeze one prediction to reconcile against measurement. Legal plans feed the recovery dossier and the capstone mesh choice.
steps: Build the `plan/` mesh validator: dense and expert ownership tables, world-size factorization, rank-coordinate maps with round trips, group construction, and invalid-product rejection tested with CPU `gloo` collectives.

Add the batch-token ledger and layout validator: unique examples and valid tokens per update, divisibility tables for heads, widths, vocabulary, sequence, layers and experts, with invalid and uneven cases refused loudly.

Extend the ledger to per-rank state, buffers and checkpoint staging with live-window peaks, then add activation lifetimes and per-stage temporary memory under the pipeline schedules you validated earlier.

Derive per-layer FLOPs and the full collective-volume ledger across data, sharded, tensor, sequence, context, pipeline and expert dimensions, then map groups onto links with a contention table; solve the CS336 data-parallel, FSDP and TP calculations and the scaling-book sharding case first.

Build the composed critical-path simulator with imbalance cases and overlap-versus-serialization bounds, then compare three workload scenarios that keep batch and update fixed while naming the assumption that reverses each winner.

Extend the planner past the TensorTonic topology cases with sharding, expert reuse and schedule costs, keeping rejection reasons and adding no-feasible-plan and tied-score tests; freeze one prediction, reconcile the largest residual with a controlled change, and test a held-out configuration.

Run the TorchFeather composed CPU example, then add a concatenated-batch oracle with update checks and negative cases in trainlab; close with bandwidth-sensitivity and heterogeneous-stage simulations reporting reversals and capacity cliffs.
deliverables: The `plan/` mesh, batch, memory, volume and critical-path ledgers with the planner and its rejection record.
CPU equivalence evidence: oracle comparisons, residual manifests with raw trials, and the held-out configuration report.
The three-scenario comparison, sensitivity report, and the composed-oracle negative cases with first-mismatch owners.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Choose a Topology-Aware Parallel Plan
checks.note: Pass the public cases in your harness; keep the simplified scorer apart from the trainlab planner.

checks.name: TorchFeather CPU example: GPipe with replicated DP
checks.note: Run the composed example on CPU; add the concatenated oracle and update checks in trainlab.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 2 parallelism calculations
checks.note: Solve the data, sharded, tensor and two-dimensional calcs on paper before trusting the ledger.

checks.name: How To Scale Your Model: sharding case
checks.note: Answer on paper first with TPU figures labeled as such; carry the comparison into trainlab.

rubric.pass: Ownership tables cover every rank once per mesh, round trips pass, and invalid products fail before group creation.
rubric.strong: Dense and expert meshes share one world with distinct reduction groups named, plus a rejected configuration per rule.

rubric.pass: Batch, state, activation and volume ledgers match independent shape counts, and peaks come from live windows.
rubric.strong: One controlled change moves the largest residual, and the held-out configuration report explains the miss.

rubric.pass: The search enumerates legal plans with rejection reasons, and the winner carries topology and batch constraints.
rubric.strong: Sensitivity and heterogeneous runs name reversals and cliffs, and losing regimes stay in the report.

rubric.pass: The concatenated-batch oracle matches one update, and a wrong denominator fails with the owner named.
rubric.strong: Negative cases cover uneven layouts and tied state, each localized to group, layout and collective order.

miniProject.feedsInto: The mesh validator, ledgers, planner and oracle feed the checkpoint restore mesh, the fleet measurements and the capstone dossier.
